name: Homemade Ranch with Homemade Mayo
desc: Buttermilk ranch with fresh dill, parsley and chives, built on a from-scratch mayo.

source.title: Homemade Ranch (with homemade mayo)
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 2 tsp fresh lemon juice or white vinegar
ingredients.item: fresh lemon juice or white vinegar

ingredients.raw: 2 cups neutral oil (such as avocado or canola)
1 cup buttermilk, plus more to thin
2 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
2 to 4 tsp fresh lemon juice, to taste

steps: Mayo: in a bowl (or a tall jar if using an immersion blender), whisk the egg yolks, Dijon mustard and 2 tsp lemon juice until smooth.

Drizzle in the oil a few drops at a time while whisking constantly. Once it starts to thicken, pour in a thin steady stream until all the oil is in and the mayo is thick and holds its shape. Whisk in the pinch of salt. Measure out 1 cup for the ranch and refrigerate the rest.
Ranch: whisk the mayo, sour cream and buttermilk in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the dill, parsley, chives, garlic powder, onion powder, 1/2 tsp salt, pepper and MSG (if using).
Thin with more buttermilk, 1 tbsp at a time, if you want a pourable dressing, and add lemon juice to taste, starting with 2 tsp.
Cover and chill at least 30 minutes before serving (overnight is better).
tips: It tastes better the next day once the herbs have time to meld.
The mayo uses raw egg yolks. Use pasteurized eggs if you are serving anyone pregnant, very young, elderly or immune-compromised, and keep the mayo and ranch refrigerated.
The mayo recipe makes about twice what the ranch needs; the extra keeps a few days in the fridge.
